trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer (Miner)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Miner creating blocks for the DAO fork. Authenticated via Proof of Work consensus but can choose block contents. Must include dao-hard-fork extraData during fork range but has flexibility in other aspects.

trusted_external_entities.name: DAO Token Holder
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Original holder of DAO tokens calling withdraw() function. No authentication beyond valid transaction signature. Cannot be assumed to have legitimate claim without verification against mainDAO token balance.

trusted_external_entities.name: PoW Miner
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Mining entity producing Proof of Work blocks. Authenticated via PoW but can manipulate timestamps within protocol bounds and has some freedom in transaction ordering. Must follow difficulty bomb delay rules.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Network Layer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Devp2p network propagating blocks between nodes. Network peers are untrusted; block data must be fully validated including PoW verification before acceptance.

trusted_external_entities.name: GraphQL Client
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External application or user querying the Ethereum node via GraphQL API. Query parameters are untrusted and can be used for DoS through expensive queries. No built-in authentication.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External user or application submitting signed transactions via GraphQL mutation. Transaction bytes are untrusted; must be RLP decoded and validated before broadcast.

trusted_external_entities.name: API Client
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External application making requests to the GraphQL API. Operations must be restricted to allowed set (queries, sendRawTransaction). Signing, compiling, and mining operations are denied by design.

trusted_external_entities.name: Sender Application
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Application holding the private key to be encapsulated and transferred. Has possession of sensitive key material. Must be trusted to perform correct ECIES encryption and destroy ephemeral keys after use.

trusted_external_entities.name: Recipient Application
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Application that will receive and store the private key. Initiates key encapsulation protocol by generating ephemeral keys. Cannot be trusted to securely store received key or destroy ephemeral material.

trusted_external_entities.name: Key Provider
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Entity providing the recipient's public key with optional signature. Public key authenticity must be verified via signature chain if provided. Without signature, trust is entirely implicit and risky.

trusted_external_entities.name: Original Key Holder
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Entity that currently holds the private key to be transferred. Trusted to initiate legitimate key transfer. Must properly destroy local copy after successful transfer to maintain security.

trusted_external_entities.name: Untrusted Transport Channel
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network or channel over which encrypted key data is transmitted. Assumed to be fully observable by attackers. ECIES encryption must protect key material against passive observation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Proof Consumer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Light client or verifier requesting merkle proofs for list elements. Proof requests are untrusted and may target arbitrary indices. Proof generation must be bounded to prevent resource exhaustion.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Token holder's DAO balance is verified against mainDAO contract. Transfer fails with exception if verification fails or transfer cannot complete.
Block number is consensus-verified. Miner cannot manipulate block number but can choose which block to mine on.
Block data from P2P network is completely untrusted. Full validation including difficulty computation and PoW verification required before acceptance.
GraphQL query syntax must be parsed and validated. Query complexity should be bounded. No authentication mechanism defined in spec; external access control required.
RLP-encoded transaction must be fully decoded and validated. Transaction signature verification is mandatory before broadcast.
API requests filtered by operation type. Signing, compiling, and mining operations are explicitly denied to prevent security risks.
Recipient initiates protocol but cannot be trusted to maintain PFS. Sender must verify signature chain if available before encapsulating sensitive key.
Sender app must use CSRNG for ephemeral key generation. Private key must be properly encrypted before transport. Ephemeral keys must be destroyed after protocol completion.
Public key authenticity is critical. Without signature verification, MITM attacks are possible. Trust chain validation recommended when available.
Key holder must securely manage key in memory. Key exposure should be minimized. Local copy must be destroyed after successful transfer.
Proof requests can target any index. Resource consumption for large indices grows logarithmically but should still be bounded. Rate limiting recommended.
